summary_paraphrase: Two king penguin chicks who do everything together walk far from their colony, laugh at an odd-looking penguin with head plumes and leave him alone; after they moult into young adults and need someone to teach them to swim, that same penguin offers, and the three swim together.

beats.function: the pair, too young to swim, walk far
a crowd of strangers, one odd bird
who will teach us? the stranger offers

characters.name: oakum boy (first)
characters.desire: to do everything together; later, to swim
characters.change: from fluffy chick who laughs at a stranger to young penguin who swims with him

characters.name: oakum boy (second)
characters.relation_to_protagonist: inseparable friend; the pair narrate as one

characters.name: (unnamed plumed penguin; the back note calls him a macaroni)
characters.change: from teased outsider to the friend who teaches them to swim
characters.relation_to_protagonist: outsider they tease; becomes their teacher and friend
characters.tension_source: his exclusion, shown only in pictures (p5-6)

humor_notes: One gentle teasing line about the stranger's head (p5); the humour is the chicks', and the picture shows it lands on someone alone.

repetition.description: two-voice exchanges: one short exclamation answered by a matching one
repetition.why: two tiny matched lines suit two reading voices and mark the pair's sameness

repetition.description: 'too young to swim' (p2) returns as the question of who will teach them (p10), paid off by swimming (p11)
repetition.why: the opening lack becomes the ending's goal, so the climax needs no explanation

repetition.description: wordless spreads alternate with text spreads (p4, p6, p8, p11, p12 are wordless)
repetition.why: the silent spreads carry the reveal, the exclusion, the moult and the reconciliation

notes: 5 of 12 spreads are wordless and they carry the moral line: the stranger left alone (p6) and the friendship (p11-12) exist only in pictures.
Read without pictures the text is a plain growing-up story; the exclusion-and-repair arc disappears.
Scale tells distance: the chicks shrink to dots on a wide ice field (p3).
The moult is drawn as a full spread of drifting feathers with no character (p8): time passing as texture.
Watercolour, lots of white page; text sits on white, never over the art.
Spoken lines carry no quotation marks, so the CLI dialogue_ratio of 0 understates speech: p5, p7, p9 and p10 are spoken.

strengths: the opening lack (too young to swim) becomes the climax's need
the outsider they mocked is the one who helps; the reversal is shown, not preached
very short lines suited to read-aloud by two voices
wordless spreads give the listener room to tell what happened
weaknesses: the pair never acknowledge or repair the teasing in words; the reconciliation is implied by pictures only
the name 'oakum boys' is explained only in the back-matter note
spoken lines carry no quotation marks or speaker tags, so who speaks on p10 depends on the picture

anti_patterns.note: 'oakum' is unknown to most 3-4 year olds and the story never explains it
the teasing is never revisited; the stranger simply volunteers

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Mild teasing of a different-looking penguin is left unrepaired in words; an adult may want to narrate the wordless spreads.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
